column1: # Fukuoka MQ Challenge: every recorded solve of all six types.
# THESE ARE PUBLISHED RESULTS, NOT INSTANCES. No challenge coefficient file and
# no answer vector is committed here; the challenge data carries no licence
# (see docs/research/fukuoka-mq.md section 3). Each row points at the page it
# was read from, which is also where that solve's answer vector can be fetched.
# `answer_values` records how many values that vector carries, which is what
# makes a truncated one visible without committing it.
# Source of record: the challenge's own "full list of all submission details",
#   sha256 of the HTML as fetched: see docs/research/fukuoka-mq.md section 0
# plus, per row, the linked per-submission page named in the `details` column,
# Types II, III, V and VI accessed 2026-11-07; types I and IV, and the
# re-derivation of the link count, 2026-11-09 against the same submissions
# One page, one row. The 125 rows here are in bijection with the 125
# `details_<TYPE>_*.html` links the submissions page carries: no page is
# unrepresented and no page is cited by two rows. An earlier count of 58 pages
# was an artefact of matching `details_<TYPE>_[0-9]{8}.html`, which drops every
# page whose name carries a `_<k>` suffix for a second submission the same day,
# and the two `_cs.html` pages. See docs/research/fukuoka-mq.md section 14.2.
# The hall of fame on the front page shows only the five highest positions per
# type; this file is the complete list. Two of the site's own rules make it an
# UNDERCOUNT of what has been solved rather than a census:
#   Rule 2 - for a given n only the first five solves are recorded;
#   Rule 3 - a participant may record at most one solve per n.
# So the absence of a row for an (n, seed) pair is not evidence that the pair
# Rows are sorted by type (site order I..VI), then n, m, seed, date.
#   type                    I to VI as the site labels it. Types I, II and III
#                           are the encryption families (m = 2n); IV, V and VI
#                           are the signature families (n = floor(1.5 m)).
#                           Types I, III, IV and VI are over GF(2); II and V
#                           over GF(2^8), which is why their answer vectors are
#                           printed as hex bytes rather than as bits.
#   n, m                    variables and polynomials, as the detail page prints
#                           them. The site indexes types I/II/III by n and types
#   date                    submission date, ISO 8601, from the detail page.
#   figure_kind             WHAT runtime_seconds measures. The site mixes four
#                           conventions and does not flag the difference:
#                             cpu-total            total CPU time, from a page
#                             per-subsystem-cpu    CPU seconds for ONE subsystem
#                             per-subsystem-wall   wall clock for ONE subsystem
#                           Neither a per-subsystem figure nor a CPU total is
#                           comparable with a wall-clock total, and neither must
#   runtime_seconds         the `Running Time` figure converted to seconds, in
#   phases_seconds          sum of the per-phase times the `Notes` field
#                           Recorded so the total can be checked against its own
#   peak_gb, peak_metric    peak memory and WHICH metric, where published. Only
#                           two rows have one, and they use different metrics
#                           (VmHWM and VmPeak), which are not the same number.
#   subsystems              number of subsystems solved before a solution was
#                           found, for the hybrid attacks that report it.
#   avg_subsystem_seconds   average time per subsystem, as reported.
#   processes               simultaneous processes, where the notes state it
#                           AND the three figures reconcile. Deliberately left
#                           `-` on three rows that state a count and an average
#                           but whose totals do not follow from them: type VI
#                           the two 2025 type VI rows (implying 7.6-way and
#                           `-` on every type I and IV row: no type I or IV page
#                           publishes a phase breakdown, a memory peak, a
#                           subsystem count or a process count. The one note
#                           that states memory at all gives the machines' RAM,
#                           which is a configuration and not a measured peak.
#   answer_published        whether the detail page prints the answer vector.
#   runtime_printed         the `Running Time` field verbatim, so the conversion
#                           in runtime_seconds can be rechecked by eye.
#   cores                   the core count the figure is on, where the `Running
#                           Time` field itself states one ("4 hours on 300
#                           cores"), else `-`. Not taken from `hardware`: a
#                           machine's core count is not evidence the run used
#   resource_hours          the aggregate resource figure the page publishes,
#   resource_metric         and which resource it counts:
#                             cpu-hours   a CPU.h or CPU-hours figure
#                             mixed       the page publishes BOTH, so no single
#                                         figure is the cost; resource_hours is
#                                         `-` and the page must be read
#                           This is the parallel cost, which a wall-clock figure
#                           on a cluster hides entirely: type I n=83 is 805000
#   answer_values           how many values the published answer vector carries.
#                           Equals n on every row but one: the type I n=75 page
#                           prints 74. Recorded rather than silently accepted.
# Nothing in this file was measured, re-run or estimated here. Every figure is
# transcribed from the page named in its `details` column.
